issues.description: The problem statement and template expect Milkable.messageOnMilk() without parameters (returning a string like "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). However, the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) and implements it with a volume parameter in Goat and Seal. This parameter mismatch between specification/template and the solution will confuse students and prevent using the solution as a correct reference (and will cause code that calls messageOnMilk() with no arguments to fail against the solution).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Change the solution to match the problem/template by declaring Milkable.messageOnMilk() with no parameters and update Goat and Seal to implement messageOnMilk() returning "[Animal Type] [name] is milked", or (B) Update the problem statement and template to require messageOnMilk(double volume) and adjust described return values and examples accordingly. Option A is likely the least disruptive to the exercise as currently described.

issues.description: The Milkable API is specified in the problem statement and used in the template as messageOnMilk() with no parameters, but the solution repository defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) (and implements it accordingly). This signature mismatch (no-arg vs. one double parameter) refers to the same conceptual operation (milking an animal) but uses different identifiers/signatures across artifacts, which will confuse students and can lead to compilation or mapping errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable API across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to match the problem/template by removing the parameter: define String messageOnMilk() in Milkable and update Seal/Goat implementations to return "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (no volume), or (B) update the problem statement and template to specify messageOnMilk(double volume) and adjust examples/usages accordingly. Option A is recommended to match the existing problem text and template usage.
